checks.claim: Microwaves bounce around inside the oven and form hot and cold spots, which is why most ovens have a turntable.
checks.why: Reflected waves interfere into standing waves with hot and cold spots about 6 cm apart; the turntable moves food through them so it heats more evenly.

sources.title: Hot spots in the microwave (TU Delft)
Why Do We Need A Turntable In Microwaves? (ScienceABC)

checks.claim: The metal mesh in a microwave's door has holes much smaller than the microwaves' wavelength of about 12 centimeters, so the waves cannot pass through.
checks.why: Microwave ovens' waves are about 12 cm long; the door mesh holes are far smaller, so the metal mesh reflects them while visible light passes.

sources.title: The mesh grating on your microwave is a safety feature (Mental Floss)

checks.claim: Microwave ovens have interlock switches that cut power to the magnetron as soon as the door opens.
checks.why: Door interlock switches stop power reaching the magnetron when the door opens; designs use two switches and a monitor switch for redundancy.

sources.title: Tech in plain sight: microwave ovens (Hackaday)
Microwave oven door interlock switch system (US patent 4096370)
